nodes.title: Rutherford's Model & Distance of Closest Approach
points: Geiger-Marsden α-scattering experiment: Most α-particles passed undeflected; ~1 in 8000 deflected by > 90°; very few retraced path (~180°).
Conclusions: Entire positive charge and nearly all mass are concentrated in an extremely dense central nucleus (< 10⁻¹⁴ m). Most of the atom is empty space (~10⁻¹⁰ m).
Distance of closest approach (head-on collision): Initial KE equals electrostatic PE at closest approach r₀: ½ m v² = (1 / 4πε₀) (2Ze² / r₀) ⟹ r₀ = (1 / 4πε₀) (2Ze² / E_k).
Impact parameter b: Perpendicular distance of initial velocity vector from central nucleus: b ∝ cot(θ/2). For head-on collision, b = 0, θ = 180°.
Limitations of Rutherford's Model: (1) Instability of atom (accelerated electron should radiate energy and spiral into nucleus); (2) Could not explain discrete line spectra.

nodes.title: Bohr's Atomic Model & Three Postulates
points: First Postulate: Electron revolves in circular orbits where necessary centripetal force is provided by electrostatic Coulomb attraction: m v² / r = (1 / 4πε₀) (Ze² / r²).

Second Postulate (Bohr's Quantization Condition): Electron can revolve only in non-radiating stable orbits where orbital angular momentum is an integral multiple of h/2π: L = m v r = n h / (2π), where n = 1, 2, 3... is Principal Quantum Number.
Third Postulate (Frequency Condition): When electron jumps from higher energy state E_i to lower state E_f, a photon of energy hν is emitted: E_i − E_f = hν = hc / λ.

nodes.title: Radii, Velocity & Energy in Bohr Orbits
points: Radius of n-th orbit: r_n = (ε₀ h² n²) / (π m Z e²) = a₀ (n² / Z). For Hydrogen (Z=1, n=1): Bohr radius a₀ = 0.529 Å = 0.0529 nm. Radius r_n ∝ n² / Z.
Speed of electron in n-th orbit: v_n = (Z e²) / (2 ε₀ n h) = v₁ (Z / n). For Hydrogen ground state: v₁ = c / 137 ≈ 2.18 × 10⁶ m/s. Speed v_n ∝ Z / n.
Kinetic Energy: KE = + (m Z² e⁴) / (8 ε₀² h² n²) = + 13.6 (Z² / n²) eV.
Potential Energy: PE = − (m Z² e⁴) / (4 ε₀² h² n²) = − 27.2 (Z² / n²) eV.
Total Energy: E_n = KE + PE = − (m Z² e⁴) / (8 ε₀² h² n²) = − 13.6 (Z² / n²) eV. Negative sign signifies bound system.
Master Energy Link: PE = 2 E_n; KE = −E_n; Total Energy E_n = −KE.

nodes.title: Hydrogen Spectral Series & Rydberg Formula
points: Rydberg Formula: Wavenumber ν̄ = 1/λ = R_H Z² (1/n₁² − 1/n₂²), where Rydberg constant R_H = (m e⁴) / (8 ε₀² h³ c) ≈ 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹.
1. Lyman Series: n₁ = 1, n₂ = 2, 3, 4... | Ultraviolet (UV) region. Shortest λ: n₂ = ∞ (λ_min = 1/R ≈ 912 Å); Longest λ: n₂ = 2 (λ_max = 4/3R ≈ 1216 Å).
2. Balmer Series: n₁ = 2, n₂ = 3, 4, 5... | VISIBLE region. First line (H_α line): n₂ = 3 (Red, λ = 6563 Å).
3. Paschen Series: n₁ = 3, n₂ = 4, 5... | Infrared (IR) region.
4. Brackett Series: n₁ = 4, n₂ = 5, 6... | Infrared (IR) region.
5. Pfund Series: n₁ = 5, n₂ = 6, 7... | Far Infrared region.
Total number of spectral lines emitted when electron de-excites from state n to ground state: N = n(n − 1) / 2.

nodes.title: Nuclear Structure, Size & Invariant Density
points: Nucleus contains protons (Z) and neutrons (N = A − Z). Mass number A = Z + N.
Isotopes: Same Z, different A (e.g., ¹H, ²H, ³H); Isobars: Same A, different Z (e.g., ⁴⁰Ar, ⁴⁰Ca); Isotones: Same neutron number N = A − Z.
Nuclear Radius: R = R₀ A^(1/3), where R₀ ≈ 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m = 1.2 fm (Fermi). Nuclear volume V ∝ R³ ∝ A.
Nuclear Density: ρ = Mass / Volume = (A × m_n) / [4/3 π (R₀ A^(1/3))³] = m_n / (4/3 π R₀³) ≈ 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³.
Crucial Fact: Nuclear density is CONSTANT and INDEPENDENT of mass number A for all nuclei.

nodes.title: Mass Defect, Binding Energy & BE/A Curve
points: Mass Defect (Δm): Difference between total mass of individual nucleons and actual rest mass of the nucleus: Δm = [Z m_p + (A − Z) m_n] − M_nucleus.
Binding Energy (BE): Energy released when nucleus is assembled from separated nucleons: BE = Δm × c² = Δm (in u) × 931.5 MeV (1 u ≈ 931.5 MeV).
Binding Energy per Nucleon (BE / A) determines nuclear stability: Higher BE/A means greater stability.
BE/A Curve Key Features: Maximum stability near iron (⁵⁶Fe, BE/A ≈ 8.79 MeV/nucleon); average value ~8.5 MeV/nucleon for 30 < A < 170; drops for light nuclei (A < 30) and heavy nuclei (A > 170).
Nuclear Fission: Heavy unstable nucleus (e.g., ²³⁵U) splits into middle fragments to increase BE/A and release energy (~200 MeV per fission).
Nuclear Fusion: Light nuclei (e.g., hydrogen isotopes) fuse to form heavier nucleus with higher BE/A, releasing immense energy (powers the Sun).

nodes.title: Radioactive Decay Law, Half-Life & Activity
points: Radioactivity is spontaneous, uncontrollable disintegration of unstable heavy nuclei with emission of α, β, or γ rays.
Radioactive Decay Law: Rate of disintegration is directly proportional to number of active nuclei present: −dN/dt = λ N ⟹ N(t) = N₀ e^(−λt).
Decay constant (λ): Fractional number of atoms disintegrating per unit time. SI unit: s⁻¹.
Half-Life (T_½): Time required for half of radioactive nuclei to decay: T_½ = ln 2 / λ = 0.693 / λ.
Mean Life (Average Life τ): Reciprocal of decay constant: τ = 1 / λ = T_½ / 0.693 ≈ 1.44 T_½.
Activity (A): Rate of decay: A(t) = −dN/dt = λ N = A₀ e^(−λt). SI unit: Becquerel (1 Bq = 1 dps). 1 Curie (Ci) = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq.
Amount remaining after n half-lives: N = N₀ (½)^n = N₀ (½)^(t / T_½).

nodes.title: Alpha, Beta, Gamma Decay & Nuclear Reactions
points: Alpha Decay: Emission of helium nucleus (⁴₂He): ^A_Z X ⟶ ^(A−4)_(Z−2) Y + ⁴₂He + Q. Mass number decreases by 4, atomic number by 2.
Beta-minus (β⁻) Decay: Neutron converts to proton: ^A_Z X ⟶ ^A_(Z+1) Y + e⁻ + ν̄_e (antineutrino). Atomic number Z increases by 1, A unchanged.
Beta-plus (β⁺) Decay: Proton converts to neutron: ^A_Z X ⟶ ^A_(Z−1) Y + e⁺ + ν_e (neutrino). Atomic number Z decreases by 1, A unchanged.
Gamma (γ) Decay: Excited nucleus transitions to lower energy state emitting high-energy photon: ^A_Z X* ⟶ ^A_Z X + γ. Z and A remain unchanged.
Nuclear Forces: Strongest attractive force in nature; short-range (~1–2 fm); charge-independent (F_pp ≈ F_nn ≈ F_pn); saturated force.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Derivations & Spectral Series
points: Board Favourite #1: State Bohr's postulates and derive expressions for radius of n-th orbit r_n = ε₀h²n²/(πmZe²) and total energy E_n = −13.6 Z²/n² eV.
Board Favourite #2: Derive Rydberg formula 1/λ = R_H (1/n₁² − 1/n₂²) for hydrogen spectral series and label Lyman, Balmer, Paschen on energy level diagram.
Board Favourite #3: State radioactive decay law and derive N(t) = N₀ e^(−λt) and half-life relation T_½ = 0.693/λ.
Board Favourite #4: Define mass defect and binding energy per nucleon; explain nuclear fission and fusion on the basis of BE/A curve.

formulas.label: Radius derivation
formulas.expr: r_n = (ε₀ h² n²) / (π m Z e²)

formulas.label: Energy derivation
formulas.expr: E_n = − (m Z² e⁴) / (8 ε₀² h² n²)

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, Orbit Traps & Decay Hacks
points: Orbit Proportionalities: Radius r ∝ n² / Z; Velocity v ∝ Z / n; Time period T = 2πr/v ∝ n³ / Z²; Frequency ν ∝ Z² / n³; Orbital current I ∝ Z² / n³; Magnetic moment M ∝ n.
Series Limit Shortcut: Series limit (shortest wavelength λ_min) occurs when n₂ = ∞ ⟹ λ_min = n₁² / R_H.
Longest Wavelength Shortcut: First line (longest wavelength λ_max) occurs when n₂ = n₁ + 1.
Balmer Series Trap: Balmer series is the ONLY series lying in the visible region. First line is red (6563 Å), second line is blue-green (4861 Å).
Half-Life Fraction Hack: After 1 T_½ ⟹ 50% left (50% decayed); 2 T_½ ⟹ 25% left (75% decayed); 3 T_½ ⟹ 12.5% left (87.5% decayed); 4 T_½ ⟹ 6.25% left (93.75% decayed).
Nuclear Radius Ratio: R₁ / R₂ = (A₁ / A₂)^(1/3).

formulas.label: Decay fraction shortcut
formulas.expr: N / N₀ = (½)^n where n = t / T_½
